name: API Design
description: Designing and evolving interfaces other software calls: REST/GraphQL/RPC endpoints, request/response contracts, versioning, and integrations. Knowing a programming language is not API Design.

name: Authentication
description: Verifying user or service identity: login flows, sessions, OAuth/OIDC/SSO, tokens, passwords, and MFA.

name: Authorization
description: Controlling what an authenticated identity may do: roles, permissions, scopes, access policies, and tenant isolation.

name: Database Design
description: Modeling data: schemas, tables, relations, indexes, migrations, and query design.

name: Idempotency
description: Making operations safe to retry or repeat without duplicate side effects: idempotency keys, deduplication, exactly-once handling.

name: Job Scheduling
description: Background and scheduled work: queues, cron jobs, workers, retries, and long-running task orchestration.

name: Observability
description: Instrumenting systems so behavior is visible: logging, metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alerting.

name: Distributed Systems
description: Designing systems that span multiple services or machines: concurrency, consistency, networking, scaling, and fault tolerance. Using a specific infrastructure tool is not by itself this capability.

name: Production Debugging
description: Diagnosing and fixing failures in live systems: incident investigation, root-cause analysis, and hotfixes.

name: CI/CD
description: Automated build, test, and deployment pipelines (for example GitHub Actions or release automation). General programming-language skill is not CI/CD.

name: Database Security (Row-Level Security)
description: Protecting data at the database layer: row-level security policies, grants, and least-privilege access.

name: Prompt/System Design
description: Designing prompts, system instructions, and model interaction flows that shape LLM behavior in a product. General familiarity with LLMs is not by itself this capability.

name: Agent Orchestration
description: Building multi-step or multi-agent LLM workflows that plan, call tools, and coordinate steps.

name: Tool Use
description: Letting models call external functions or APIs (function calling, tool schemas) and handling the results.

name: Evaluation
description: Measuring AI/model output quality: evals, test sets, benchmarks, graders, and regression testing of model behavior.

name: RAG
description: Retrieval-augmented generation: embeddings, vector search, and grounding model answers in retrieved documents.

name: Model Routing
description: Choosing among models or providers per request based on cost, latency, or quality, including fallbacks.

name: Structured Extraction
description: Using models to turn unstructured text into validated structured data (schemas, JSON outputs, field extraction).

name: AI-Assisted Development
description: Using AI coding tools (copilots, code assistants) to build software faster. Not the same as building AI systems or knowing a language.

name: Customer Discovery
description: Interviewing and learning from users or customers to find problems and needs.

name: Requirements
description: Turning needs into clear specs, user stories, and acceptance criteria.

name: Prioritization
description: Deciding what to build next by weighing impact, effort, and tradeoffs.

name: Prototyping
description: Quickly building mockups or throwaway versions to test ideas.

name: Launch
description: Releasing products or features to users: rollout planning, go-to-market coordination, and launch execution.

name: Iteration
description: Improving a shipped product based on feedback, data, and results.

name: Research
description: Investigating markets, competitors, or industries to inform decisions.

name: Strategy
description: Setting direction: goals, positioning, and competitive choices.

name: Communication
description: Explaining ideas clearly to stakeholders in writing, presentations, and meetings.

name: Sales
description: Selling to customers: prospecting, pitching, negotiating, closing, and growing accounts.

name: Operations
description: Running and improving business processes, logistics, and day-to-day execution.

name: Analysis
description: Analyzing business data or problems to produce conclusions and recommendations.

name: Literature Analysis
description: Reviewing and critically synthesizing published research and sources.

name: Data Collection
description: Gathering data through surveys, experiments, scraping, or fieldwork.

name: Experimental Design
description: Designing controlled studies or experiments: hypotheses, variables, and controls.

name: Statistical Interpretation
description: Applying statistics to data and correctly interpreting the results.

name: Synthesis
description: Combining findings from multiple sources into coherent insights.

name: Design
description: Visual, UX, or product design: layouts, interfaces, and graphics.

name: Writing
description: Producing clear written content such as articles, copy, and documentation.

name: Storytelling
description: Crafting narratives that engage an audience.

name: Content Production
description: Producing media content (video, audio, social) end to end.
